21. Case study: glucose trajectories

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-21-case-glucose.Rmd
book-21-case-glucose.Rmd

What you will learn

Choose a populated glucose measurement, describe trajectories and observed target attainment, and fit a small Gaussian model.

You need: the installed packages and practice resources, concept discovery, and the preceding tutorial chapters. Run these sections in order in a fresh book-work session. All observations are public synthetic teaching data; the numerical results are not clinical evidence.

Research question

Among Synthea people with blood-glucose measurements, how do first and last values relate, and when is a declared teaching target first observed? We select a lab-defined population, not a diagnosis-confirmed diabetes cohort.

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- book_connect("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns

Find the exact glucose concept 

hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Glucose", domain = "Measurement", vocabulary = "LOINC", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(hits[c("concept_name", "standard_concept", "concept_class_id")])
concept_name standard_concept concept_class_id
Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood S Lab Test
Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma S Lab Test
Glucose [Presence] in Urine by Test strip S Lab Test
Glucose [Mass/volume] in Urine by Test strip S Lab Test 
glucose_id <- hits$concept_id[trimws(hits$concept_name) == "Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood"]
knitr::kable(ds.omop.concept.locate(glucose_id, scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled)
concept_id table_name concept_column n_records n_persons
3000483 measurement measurement_concept_id 225 10 
knitr::kable(ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = glucose_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled)
n concept_name value
225 milligram per deciliter 8840 
mapping <- ds.omop.concept.relationships(glucose_id, relationship_id = "Maps to",
  conns = conns, symbol = "omop")$pooled
children <- ds.omop.concept.descendants(glucose_id, include_self = FALSE,
  conns = conns, symbol = "omop")$pooled
print(data.frame(Maps_to_rows = NROW(mapping), Descendant_rows = NROW(children)))
#>   Maps_to_rows Descendant_rows
#> 1            2               0
glucose_set <- omop_concept_set(glucose_id)

This populated Blood concept differs from Serum or Plasma. Its recorded unit is mg/dL. The categories below are public teaching thresholds, not treatment advice.

Cohort, values and trajectories 

glucose <- omop_event("measurement", glucose_set, unit = omop_unit(8840L))
first <- omop_variable(event = glucose, reducer = omop_reduce("first_value"))
last <- omop_variable(event = glucose, reducer = omop_reduce("last_value"))
cohort <- omop_population("measured", index = omop_index(glucose))
trajectory <- omop_recipe(populations = list(cohort), variables = list(
  first = first, last = last,
  control = omop_number_category(last, range = "thresholds", thresholds = c(70, 140)),
  change = omop_number_change(glucose),
  target_days = omop_number_change(glucose, "time_to_threshold", threshold = 140, op = "le")),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "measured", format = "wide"))
book_symbols(recipe_execute(trajectory, out = c(people = "D_glucose"), conns = conns))
#>      people 
#> "D_glucose"
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_glucose$change", datasources = conns)))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% -25.715
site 10% -23.330
site 25% -15.275
site 50% 9.050
site 75% 18.900
site 90% 23.130
site 95% 25.965
site Mean 2.580

All available history contributes to first and last. A difference in person-level values is not a slope or an intervention effect. Selecting people with a test can also select on disease severity and healthcare use.

Categories and time to target

The prescribed three-level rule produces a small category in this tiny sample. This deliberately shows a refusal: the table is withheld, not a zero-frequency result. Keep the planned thresholds and report that limitation.

control_message <- tryCatch(ds.omop.table("D_glucose", "control", conns = conns),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
print(control_message)
#> [1] "Every retained site must release a valid ds.table; pooled table refused."

An observed target time is missing for someone never observed below the threshold. Day zero means already meeting it at the first reading. Measurement schedules can move observed attainment later than the underlying biological change.

knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_glucose$target_days", datasources = conns)))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% 0
site 10% 0
site 25% 0
site 50% 0
site 75% 0
site 90% 0
site 95% 0
site Mean 0

Model the last value

Fit last glucose against first glucose. This small synthetic Gaussian model teaches a workflow; it is not a validated diabetes risk model. The local-start warnings are the documented dsBase setup behaviour, not hidden output.

glucose_fit <- dsBaseClient::ds.glm("last ~ first", data = "D_glucose",
  family = "gaussian", datasources = conns)
#> Warning: glm.fit: algorithm did not converge
#> Warning: glm.fit: algorithm did not converge
#> Warning: glm.fit: algorithm did not converge
#> Warning: glm.fit: algorithm did not converge
knitr::kable(glucose_fit$coefficients)

Exercises

1. Summarise first glucose in its declared unit.

Solution 1

knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_glucose$first", datasources = conns)))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% 68.320
site 10% 69.940
site 25% 78.275
site 50% 84.550
site 75% 90.050
site 90% 92.980
site 95% 96.040
site Mean 83.400

The unit is mg/dL. A unit declaration must match the recorded source.

2. Explain why target-time missingness should not be replaced with zero.

Solution 2

trajectory$variables$target_days$derived[c("method", "threshold", "op", "reference")]
#> $method
#> [1] "time_to_threshold"
#> 
#> $threshold
#> [1] 140
#> 
#> $op
#> [1] "le"
#> 
#> $reference
#> [1] "first"

Zero represents immediate observed attainment. Missing instead means no observed attainment in the eligible records; a censored analysis needs follow-up times too.

3. Inspect the fitted sample size and convergence information.

Solution 3

glucose_fit[c("Nvalid", "Nmissing", "iter", "errorMessage")]
#> $Nvalid
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $Nmissing
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $iter
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $errorMessage
#>      ERROR MESSAGES
#> site "No errors"

A successful recipe does not guarantee enough complete observations for a model. Keep diagnostics beside the coefficients in a study record.

Recap

Find a populated measurement, state the selected population, define units and thresholds, preserve temporal meaning, then interpret a model within those choices. Rare categories and small complete-case samples can limit what is releasable.
